 Broad money growth accelerated sharply in September 2026 compared to the corresponding period of the
previous year. Both net foreign assets and net domestic assets contributed, although NFA growth far
outpaced NDA growth.
 Public sector credit rose sharply within domestic credit, primarily due to increased government
borrowing. Private sector credit growth remained below 5 percent in September 2026.
 Among M2 components, currency outside banks grew faster than deposits, consistent with the trend
observed throughout the year.

 Reserve money growth in September 2026 eased a bit after a sharp jump in August 2026 and a marked
turnaround from below 4 percent growth recorded a year earlier. Bangladesh Bank's net foreign assets
remained the key driver of this growth.
 Net domestic assets growth of Bangladesh Bank declined again in September 2026 after a slight positive
growth in the previous month. The money multiplier eased slightly from its year-earlier level.
